content.title: Celebrating authors around the world
content.summary: AKU campuses mark second annual Author's Day with fun and engaging activities

content.text: The Aga Khan University Library hosted its second annual Author's Day to celebrate authors and writers across its campuses.

"International Authors' Day is an important event, particularly as we acknowledge writers and appreciate their hard work. We intend to nurture efforts that inspire authorship through engagements with authors and publishers," said Associate Vice Provost and University Librarian Dr Peter Gatiti.

Across AKU campuses in East Africa, Pakistan and the United Kingdom, the day began with a book swap and 'free library' activity. Faculty, staff and students were encouraged to either donate a book or exchange with a colleague. This was aimed at encouraging a reading culture at the University.

In Nairobi, a panel discussion was held with keynote speaker Ambassador Prof Bitange Ndemo, Kenya's Ambassador to Belgium. Together with AKU faculty, they offered insights and practical tips from their authorship and publishing journey.

The panel discussions also took place in Kampala and Dar es Salaam with Joseph Mwizerwa, Associate Dean, School of Nursing and Midwifery East Africa and Prof Eunica Siaity-Pallangyo, Associate Regional Provost, Tanzania as keynote speakers respectively.

Eighteen AKU authors from Kenya who had more than 50 publications in the University's Institutional Repository eCommons were awarded, while in Tanzania, six authors were awarded for having more than 30 publications. In Uganda, five were awarded. This was to recognize and celebrate their efforts in research and creating new knowledge. eCommons currently has a total of 19,510 scholarly publications with over 2.4 million downloads.
In Karachi, the celebrations started a day earlier with a two-day book exhibition where eight prominent publishing houses and book sellers displayed a wide range of books.

Later on, two panel discussions chaired by Dr Anjum Halai, Vice Provost and Founding Dean, Faculty of Arts and Sciences and Dr Adil Haider, Dean of the Medical College analysed various publications by AKU authors.

In London, the book swap brought together institutions within the Aga Khan Centre: the Institute for Muslim Civilizations, the Institute for Ismaili Studies and the Aga Khan Foundation. Later in the day, journalist and commentator Remona Aly talked about her role as part of a game-changing generation of young Muslims reaching out to a broader audience.
The Author's Day events were organised by the Office of the University Librarian and will continue to be celebrated every year on November 1.
